video_title: I Got a 96% WIN Rate with this BROKEN Deck

bullets: Game 3 of 8 in the video, a win over Golem beatdown (Elixir Collector, Baby Dragon, Witch, Graveyard, a mirror Ronin, Berserker, Vines). Won essentially in the first 25 seconds and then held on: a split Wall Breakers opening plus Goblin Barrel onto the Elixir Collector and a Ronin behind it took the enemy right tower 4858 -> 1661 HP by clock 2:25, and the only other offence all game was one Barrel + Wall Breakers cycle at clock 1:09 (enemy left 4265 -> 1801).

Piloted as bait that spends most of its cards on defence: from clock 2:00 onward Wall Breakers, Skeletons and Fire Spirit are all used as kites and pulls rather than as threats ("go for a Wall Breakers to kite the Roane", t=399; "go for the skeletons to kite this in", t=392; "Fire spirit like this. Bring this over", t=468), with Royal Delivery as the closer on top of an already-committed defence (t=394.7, t=454.6, t=465.5, t=481.5).

Tesla is the backbone against the tank: five placements in 173 seconds, all in tiles [8-10] rows 9-10, deliberately high to drag the Golem across the arena — "it's going to pull the Golem really, really far and it's going to start shooting it a little bit earlier than a normal Tesla placement ... since the Tesla got that lifetime nerf, it can be a little bit sketchy to have to pre-place Teslas. But with my card cycle, I kind of had to" (t=372-385).

The cheap cycle is treated as a resource in its own right: he barrels to reach the Evolution ("I need to cycle and apply some pressure. Getting to the Evo Wall Breakers will be super nice as well", t=434-437), and he banks elixir instead of over-defending when the read allows it (declines a second Magic Archer at t=419, waits on a second Elixir Collector at t=429).

Magic Archer is the Hero variant here: parked in the back-left corner both times he plays it (clock 1:57, clock 0:57) to pierce the whole Golem stack, with the 2-elixir 'Triple Threat' reposition declined once at clock 1:16 and spent at clock 0:38 to save it ("we need to step back here to keep the marcher alive. I need that to live", t=463).

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Skeletons and Fire Spirit all bait the same small spell, and at 2.88 average elixir the deck rebuilds that bait faster than the opponent can answer it.
new_deck.why_it_works_md:
The deck wins the opening exchange and then refuses to give the tower back. Wall Breakers, Goblin Barrel and Ronin land enough damage in one uncontested cycle to take a tower most of the way down (enemy right 4858 -> 1661 HP inside 25 seconds in this game), after which the same cheap cards become defensive bodies: Wall Breakers and Skeletons kite ground threats backwards, Fire Spirit drags support troops off-lane, and Royal Delivery finishes whatever the kite leaves behind.

Tesla is the anchor against tanks and is played high on purpose so it pulls a Golem far off the tower and starts firing early; Ryley notes the lifetime nerf makes that pre-placement risky, but the cheap cycle forces it and also lets it be replaced every 20-30 seconds. Magic Archer, in his Hero variant, sits in the back corner and pierces the whole push, with the 2-elixir 'Triple Threat' reposition available to save him from a spell or a closing melee unit.

The weakness is that almost nothing here kills a tank quickly, so against Golem beatdown the plan is explicitly to survive on kites and elixir efficiency rather than to trade pushes — Ryley takes chip damage on both towers all game and still wins on the lead he built in the first cycle.
